disclaimer: Deadlines and amounts are as published in the sources checked on 2026-11-11. Settlement terms change, courts move dates, and claims are judged on the official site's rules, not this feed. Always verify on the official settlement site before filing. Filing a class action typically pays 6-18 months after filing - this is 2027 money, not fast cash. Where two aggregator sites disagreed on an amount, this file uses the official-site figure and says so in the note.

entries.filingNote: $20.5M fund (Brewer v. CVS Pharmacy and Criteo, Case No. CACE-26-008094, Broward County FL). One claim per household. Final approval hearing Dec 1, 2026; payment only after approval and appeals. Amounts may shrink pro rata.
entries.linkCheck: 2026-11-11: automated curl returned 403 (bot guard); domain confirmed against the official settlement site text and three independent sources the same day.
entries.name: CVS Digital Privacy - Brewer v. CVS Pharmacy and Criteo
entries.payout: Up to $5 with no proof (Cash Payment B); up to $10 with proof of class membership (Cash Payment A)
entries.proofRequired: No - for the $5 tier. Yes - proof of class membership for the $10 tier.
entries.whoFits: Anyone in the US who accessed CVS digital properties (cvs.com, cvshealth.com, the CVS app) before July 27, 2026. No purchase required.

entries.filingNote: $6.1M fund (In re Laboratory Services Cooperative Data Breach Litigation, No. 2:25-cv-00685-BJR, W.D. Wash.). Administrator Angeion Group. Final approval hearing Jan 4, 2027. NOTE: one aggregator calendar lists this as '$300' - the official site and its detail pages say the pro-rata cash payment is capped at $1,000 per person; use the official figure.
entries.name: LSC Lab Data Breach - Laboratory Services Cooperative / Planned Parenthood lab
entries.payout: Pro-rata cash payment up to $1,000, no proof; up to $5,000 for documented out-of-pocket losses; plus 2 years of credit/medical monitoring
entries.proofRequired: No - for the pro-rata cash payment. Yes - documents for the out-of-pocket-losses tier.
entries.whoFits: US residents whose personal information was potentially compromised in the LSC data breach discovered on or about Oct 27, 2024 - including people who had lab tests ordered by a Planned Parenthood health center (or paid for someone else's) on or before Oct 27, 2024, and LSC employees.

entries.filingNote: $9M fund (Guzman et al. v. Dr. Squatch, LLC, Case No. 25STCV03523, LA County Superior Court). One claim per household. Final approval hearing Mar 2, 2027.
entries.linkCheck: 2026-11-11: HTTP 200 via curl. This row was an unverified placeholder in the Oct 25 dataset - now verified.
entries.name: Dr. Squatch - 'natural' label settlement
entries.payout: $0.50 per product: up to $2.50 with no proof (5 products); up to $12.50 with receipts (25 products total)
entries.proofRequired: No - up to 5 products on your word alone. Receipts only if claiming more than 5 products.
entries.whoFits: Anyone who bought Dr. Squatch products labeled 'natural' (soap, body wash, deodorant, shampoo, cologne, beard oil, toothpaste) in the US between Nov 1, 2018 and Aug 29, 2026.

entries.filingNote: $30M fund (Hines v. Equifax Information Services LLC, No. 1:19-cv-06701, E.D.N.Y.). Administrator Continental DataLogix. Opt-out/objection deadline Nov 20, 2026. Final approval hearing Dec 10, 2026. This row was an unverified placeholder in the Oct 25 dataset - now verified.
entries.linkCheck: 2026-11-11: automated curl returned 403 (bot guard); domain confirmed against the official settlement site and three independent sources the same day.
entries.name: Equifax - hard-inquiry dispute settlement (Hines v. Equifax)
entries.payout: Estimated about $100, $300 or $400 depending on the group Equifax's records place you in - estimates from the official site, NOT guaranteed amounts
entries.proofRequired: Claim Number + PIN from your notice; sworn certification. No receipts. If you never got a notice, check eligibility on the official site - you may not be in the class.
entries.whoFits: ONLY people whose hard-inquiry disputes are in Equifax's records: Certified Group - mailed disputes received Oct 4, 2016-Mar 27, 2026 that Equifax coded 'not mine' or 'unauthorized'; General Dispute Group - hard-inquiry disputes received Aug 31, 2021-Mar 27, 2026. Having a hard inquiry alone does NOT qualify you.

entries.filingNote: $250M fund (Landsheft v. Apple Inc., No. 5:25-cv-02668-NW, N.D. Cal.). Claims opened Sep 21, 2026. Final approval hearing Feb 24, 2027. Do NOT confuse with the Lopez v. Apple Siri privacy case ($95M) - that one closed Jul 2, 2025; see the warning row at the end of this file.
entries.linkCheck: 2026-11-11: automated curl returned 403 (bot guard); domain confirmed against the official settlement site, CNET reporting and three independent sources the same day.
entries.name: Apple Siri AI / Apple Intelligence advertising - Landsheft v. Apple
entries.payout: $25 per eligible device estimated, adjustable up to $95 or down below $25 pro rata depending on how many valid claims are filed
entries.proofRequired: No receipt - the claim runs on the device serial number.
entries.whoFits: Anyone who bought an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, iPhone 16, iPhone 16e, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16 Pro or iPhone 16 Pro Max in the US between Jun 10, 2024 and Mar 29, 2025, not for resale.

The claim deadline is Dec 28, 2026 per the settlement's date list. Final approval hearing Jan 4, 2027. Confirm both dates on the official site before filing.
entries.linkCheck: 2026-11-11: automated curl returned 403 (bot guard); domain and dates confirmed against the official settlement site as quoted by two independent sources the same day.

entries.filingNote: $32M fund (Doe v. GoodRx Holdings, Inc., No. 4:23-cv-00501-AMO, N.D. Cal.). Administrator A.B. Data. Preliminary approval Sep 8, 2026; final approval hearing Feb 11, 2027. NOTE: one aggregator calendar lists this as '$40' - the official FAQ says the per-person amount is not yet known; use the official wording, not the $40 estimate.
entries.name: GoodRx Privacy - Doe v. GoodRx Holdings
entries.payout: An equal share of the net settlement fund - amount NOT yet known (the official FAQ says 'it is not known precisely how much' each person will get)
entries.proofRequired: Claim form only - no documents listed on the official site. The claims team contacts you if your form has a problem; you then have 20 days to fix it.
entries.whoFits: People in the US who used any GoodRx website, app or service (including GoodRx Gold, HeyDoctor and GoodRx Care) at any time before Apr 20, 2024.

entries.filingNote: $167.5M fund - Visa $88.775M + Mastercard $78.725M (Burke v. Visa Inc., No. 1:11-cv-01882, D.D.C.). Preliminary approval Aug 14, 2026; claims opened Sep 11, 2026. Opt-out/objection deadline Dec 11, 2026. Final approval hearing Feb 17, 2027. This is a DIFFERENT case from the older Mackmin bank-ATM settlement (ATMClassAction.com), which closed to new claims in Jan 2025 - do not mix them up.
entries.name: Non-Bank ATM Surcharge - Burke v. Visa / Mastercard
entries.payout: A pro-rata share of the fund - amount unknown; the official site says 'nobody can know in advance how much the payment will be'
entries.proofRequired: No documents to file - you certify the claim truthfully. The administrator may ask for bank statements later.
entries.whoFits: Anyone charged a fee to take cash from their own deposit account with an ATM or PIN-debit card at an independent (non-bank) ATM in the US between Oct 24, 2007 and Aug 14, 2026, where the fee was not fully paid back by their bank. Bank-owned ATMs are NOT covered here.

entries.filingNote: Lopez v. Apple, the $95M Siri privacy case (unintended Siri recordings, Sep 17, 2014-Dec 31, 2024), closed claims on Jul 2, 2025. Final reissued payments went out Sep 21, 2026 and had to be cashed by Nov 5, 2026. No new claims, no reissue requests. If a site tells you to 'claim the $95 Apple Siri settlement' in Nov 2026, it is pointing at a closed case - the open Apple case is Landsheft (see above).
